name: nejm
description: The NEJM connector grounds AI-powered experiences in trusted, peer-reviewed evidence from the New England Journal of Medicine. Responses are informed by published research and clinical insights, with clear citations and links to the original source where available. By connecting AI-generated answers to authoritative medical literature, the NEJM connector helps clinicians and researchers verify information and make evidence-informed decisions with confidence.

publication.release_notes: This is the initial release of the NEJM connector. It grounds AI-powered experiences in trusted, peer-reviewed evidence from the *New England Journal of Medicine*. Responses are informed by published research and clinical insights, with clear citations and links to the original source where available. By connecting AI-generated answers to authoritative medical literature, the NEJM connector helps clinicians and researchers verify information and make evidence-informed decisions with confidence.

positive.description: A clinician, pharmacist, or researcher who wants published safety evidence on a drug
positive.prompt: What does the New England Journal of Medicine report about the adverse events of SGLT2 inhibitors in adults with type 2 diabetes, such as ketoacidosis, genital infections, amputation and acute kidney injury?
positive.expected_behavior: Return of relevant New England Journal of Medicine articles, mostly large trials comparing diabetes drugs called SGLT2 inhibitors with a placebo. They should answer all four parts of the question: Genital infections were clearly more common with the drugs. Ketoacidosis was rare but higher in several trials. Amputation risk was raised in only one trial of one drug, and kidney injury was not increased.

positive.description: A clinician-educator or medical writer wants to verify a claim, or look up a specific piece of data
positive.prompt: In DAPA-HF, what was the hazard ratio for the primary composite outcome of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death with dapagliflozin versus placebo in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction?
positive.expected_behavior: The tool returns the data from the original NEJM trial report (https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa1911303), with the confidence interval, the patient numbers and a citation to check against. A 2020 editorial also confirms the result. The results might also include other trial results, which tested the same drug in a different population and reported a different hazard ratio, but they should not provide the source of the data.

positive.description: A cardiology fellow wants to look at real trial data to compare different drugs
positive.prompt: How do the pivotal randomized trials of direct oral anticoagulants compare with warfarin for stroke prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, in terms of stroke or systemic embolism, major bleeding, and intracranial hemorrhage?
positive.expected_behavior: The tool returns results from the four pivotal trials, RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE and ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48, (published 2009–2013). The user gets each trial’s headline results. ChatGPT should note that the design and dosing of some of the trials differ, so a direct comparison isn’t possible.

positive.description: Any user of the Connector wanting to understand what limits the Connector might have
positive.prompt: Do I have any usage limits on the NEJM connector?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls the usage limit tool and tells the user their access status, including that no search limit currently applies. This lets users plan long research sessions without worrying about running out of searches.

positive.description: A researcher wants to understand what peer-reviewed research there is on a particular drug/disease combination
positive.prompt: What’s the evidence for GLP-1s in weight loss in patients with HFpEF
positive.expected_behavior: Return relevant NEJM research on GLP-1 therapies, weight loss, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Summarize the studied populations, interventions, weight-loss outcomes, and reported heart-failure outcomes using retrieved evidence, with citations and links to the original articles. Explain evidence limitations and distinguish findings in different populations; do not invent results or present personalized treatment advice.

negative.prompt: Find the latest peer-reviewed research on perovskite solar cells.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not invoke any NEJM connector tools. Explain that the connector covers clinical and biomedical literature from NEJM and cannot adequately research this topic.

negative.prompt: Using only the NEJM connector, summarize this Clinical Science article: https://doi.org/10.1042/CS20220797
negative.expected_behavior: Do not invoke any NEJM connector tools. Explain that this article is outside the connector’s collection. Ask the user to provide the article text; do not substitute findings from other articles or invent a summary.

negative.prompt: Upgrade my NEJM connector account to a paid plan and charge my saved payment method.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not invoke any NEJM connector tools. Explain that the connector cannot manage subscriptions or process payments. Do not claim an upgrade or charge occurred.
